# Pan-cancer differential selection across immune subtypes (Fig. 5a)

To characterize immune-associated differential selection at the pan-cancer level,
we pooled tumor samples across cancer types (**8,253 tumors across 27 TCGA cancer
types**) rather than analyzing each tumor type separately. Starting from the 299
driver genes of Bailey et al., each gene was tested for differential selection
between each immune subtype and all remaining subtypes (Thorsson **C1–C4,
one-vs-rest**), adjusting for patient age, sex, and tumor type (sex dropped for
single-sex cohorts, tumor type for single-tumor cohorts). The Benjamini–Hochberg
FDR was computed separately across all genes **within each immune subtype**.

Pipeline (see `code/`): `run_cohort_multi.R` / `recover_cohort.R` run the 299
gene-cohorts; `aggregate_pancancer299.R` combines the per-cohort C1–C4 results
into `data/pancancer299_immune_aggregated.txt`.

```{r load}
suppressMessages(library(data.table)); library(ggplot2); library(DT)
agg       <- fread("data/pancancer299_immune_aggregated.txt")
n_genes   <- length(unique(agg$gene))
sig       <- agg[dd.fdr < 0.1]
sig_genes <- sort(unique(sig$gene))
cat("Driver genes tested:", n_genes, "\n")
cat("Genes with FDR < 0.1 in >=1 immune subtype:", length(sig_genes),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * length(sig_genes) / n_genes))
cat("Significant genes:", paste(sig_genes, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

**18 of 220 driver genes (8.2%)** show differential selection across immune
subtypes.

## Fig. 5a — landscape of differential selection

Each dot is a significant gene × immune-subtype association (BH FDR < 0.1); dot
size is the significance and color indicates whether selection is stronger inside
that subtype or in the remaining subtypes.

```{r fig5a, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.8}
d <- copy(sig)
d[, subtype := factor(phenotype, levels = c("C4", "C3", "C2", "C1"))]
gord <- d[, .(m = min(dd.fdr)), by = gene][order(m), gene]
d[, gene := factor(gene, levels = gord)]
d[, dir := factor(direction, levels = c("up_in_subtype", "up_in_rest"))]
ggplot(d, aes(gene, subtype)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = -log10(dd.fdr), color = dir)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(up_in_subtype = "#B2182B", up_in_rest = "#2166AC"),
                     labels = c("stronger in subtype", "stronger in rest"),
                     name = "Direction", na.value = "grey60") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), name = expression(-log[10]~FDR)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Immune subtype") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Significant gene × subtype associations

```{r table}
datatable(
  sig[, .(gene, subtype = phenotype, dd.p = signif(dd.p, 3),
          dd.fdr = signif(dd.fdr, 3), direction, mut_freq)][order(subtype, dd.fdr)],
  options = list(pageLength = 20)
)
```
